exam: A 30‑year‑old East African man presents with facial flushing after a glass of beer – what enzyme defect explains this and what counseling would you give? — ALDH2 deficiency; advise limited alcohol, discuss cancer risk.

A patient ingests homemade spirit, now has visual blurring and high‑anion‑gap acidosis – what is the next step? — Administer fomepizole (or ethanol) and arrange haemodialysis; explain ALDH’s role in converting formaldehyde to formic acid.

Why is disulfiram used in alcohol dependence and what adverse effect would you monitor? — It irreversibly inhibits ALDH, causing acetaldehyde buildup; monitor for severe flushing, hypotension, and hepatic toxicity.
How does the ALDH2*2 polymorphism affect response to nitroglycerin? — Reduced ALDH2 activity impairs nitroglycerin bio‑activation, leading to poorer vasodilation; consider alternative anti‑anginals.
A newborn fails to thrive and has seizures; labs show low pyridoxine levels – which ALDH enzyme is implicated? — ALDH7A1 deficiency (pyridoxine‑dependent epilepsy); treat with high‑dose pyridoxine.

In a patient with chronic heavy drinking, what laboratory pattern suggests ALDH overload? — Elevated serum acetaldehyde (if measured) or persistent AST>ALT with macro‑steatosis; focus on abstinence and liver support.

Explain why a patient with sickle cell disease might have increased oxidative stress related to ALDH. — Repeated hemolysis releases heme‑derived aldehydes; ALDH detoxifies them; deficiency worsens vaso‑occlusion.
During a malaria outbreak, a patient receives artesunate and later develops hemolysis – could ALDH be involved? — No direct link; differentiate from G6PD deficiency; ALDH not implicated.
ai.title: Aldehyde Dehydrogenase (ALDH) in Metabolism
ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: ALDH enzymes oxidise toxic aldehydes (acetaldehyde, formaldehyde, 4‑HNE) to less harmful acids, protecting cells. Deficiency or inhibition leads to accumulation, causing clinical syndromes such as alcohol intolerance, hepatic injury and neurotoxicity.

b: Ubiquitous in liver, heart, brain, and erythrocytes
Key for ethanol, methanol, and lipid peroxidation product detoxification
sections.p: Aldehyde dehydrogenases are a family of NAD⁺‑dependent enzymes that convert aldehydes to carboxylic acids. The most clinically relevant isoforms are cytosolic ALDH1 (retinal metabolism) and mitochondrial ALDH2 (acetaldehyde clearance).

b: Requires NAD⁺ and a catalytic cysteine residue
Mitochondrial ALDH2 has a high Vmax for acetaldehyde
sections.p: ALDH catalyses the oxidation of an aldehyde (R‑CHO) to a carboxylic acid (R‑COOH) using NAD⁺ → NADH + H⁺. In ethanol metabolism, alcohol dehydrogenase makes acetaldehyde; ALDH2 rapidly converts it to acetate, preventing toxic buildup.
ALDH activity is modulated by genetic polymorphisms, substrate availability, and inhibition by drugs (e.g., disulfiram) or oxidative stress.

b: ALDH2 deficiency → alcohol‑induced flushing, increased cancer risk
Severe ALDH inhibition (methanol poisoning) → formic acid accumulation → optic nerve damage
sections.p: Deficiency or inhibition leads to aldehyde accumulation, causing cellular injury, oxidative stress and organ dysfunction.

b: Disulfiram blocks ALDH → aversive reaction to alcohol
Fomepizole inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, sparing ALDH in methanol/ethylene glycol poisoning
ALDH2 genotype guides risk counseling for alcohol‑related cancers
sections.p: Understanding ALDH informs management of toxic alcohol ingestions, alcohol‑related liver disease, and pharmacogenomics of drugs metabolised by aldehyde pathways.

t.b: Confirms excessive aldehyde accumulation; high levels support ALDH deficiency in acute intoxication; not routinely available – rely on clinical flushing and history
Detects metabolic acidosis from formic acid in methanol poisoning; if unavailable, assess visual symptoms and high‑anion‑gap acidosis clinically
Predicts risk of alcohol‑induced flushing and cancer; not essential for acute care, but useful for counseling

b: Remember ALDH2 converts acetaldehyde → acetate; inhibition causes flushing
Methanol → formaldehyde → formic acid; ALDH converts formaldehyde → formic acid
sections.p: Focus on enzyme pathway, clinical consequences of deficiency, and emergency management of toxic alcohols.
